Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=8}}, he played at the [[small forward]] and [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions. In [[2009–10 Euroleague|2010]], he was the [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]] winner and a member of the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]]. Kleiza represented the senior [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuanian national basketball team]] in international competitions. He led them to a bronze medal in the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], and was chosen to the All-Tournament Team. He also won a silver medal in the [[EuroBasket 2013]], earning an [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-EuroBasket Team]] selection, and a bronze medal in the [[EuroBasket 2007]]. ==Early years== Kleiza was born in Kaunas, Lithuania. At 16 years old he moved to the United States where he attended [[Montrose Christian School]] and graduated in 2003. He played on the Lithuanian Junior National Team that won the silver medal at the [[2003 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2003 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]. He led the tournament in scoring, averaging 29.1 points per game on 58 percent shooting.{{citation needed|date=March 2020}} As a senior, he was named a third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. ==College career== Kleiza played [[college basketball]] for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. He was named Honorable Mention All-Big 12 by the league coaches as a sophomore.{{cite web |title=Phillips 66 Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2005/3/7/1520359.aspx |website=big12sports.com |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=March 7, 2005}} He also earned All-Tournament honors at the [[2005 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|2005 Big 12 tournament]] after averaging 29.5 points and 9 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=2005 Phillips 66 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament All-Tournament Team |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2005/3/14/1520425.aspx |website=big12sports.com |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=March 14, 2005}} ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets=== Kleiza was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 27th pick of the [[2005 NBA draft]]. The Trail Blazers then dealt his draft rights, along with [[Ricky Sanchez]] to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Jarrett Jack]]. Kleiza was seldom used in his rookie season. He averaged 3.5 points and 8.5 minutes per game. He improved on his three-point shooting in his sophomore year, making 83–221, after only making two three-pointers in his rookie year. He also saw some more time on the court and averaged 7.6 points on 42 percent shooting in 18.8 minutes per game. After the season, Denver picked up their team option on his contract for another season. Kleiza became a big part of Denver's rotation in the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], mostly backing up Denver's starting [[small forward]] [[Carmelo Anthony]]. However, he was involved in a lot of trade talks, most notably a trade involving [[Ron Artest]] of the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |last1=Sanzharov |first1=Andrei |title=NBA Trade Rumors: Ron Artest to the Nuggets for Kleiza and Najera? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/8586-nba-trade-rumors-ron-artest-to-the-nuggets-for-kleiza-and-najera |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091206051613/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/8586-nba-trade-rumors-ron-artest-to-the-nuggets-for-kleiza-and-najera |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 6, 2009 |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=February 4, 2008}} On January 17, 2008, Kleiza scored a career high 41 points against the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |title=Nuggets' Kleiza drops in 41 points in easy win over Jazz |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280117007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817080633/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280117007 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 17, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=January 17, 2018}} His scoring average was up to 11.1 points per game and his shooting percentage was up to 47 percent. Many expected Kleiza to make a similar leap in production in his fourth year in the league. However, most of his season averages were slightly off from the 2007–08 season. He averaged 9.9 points on 45 percent shooting. His minutes dwindled down in the playoffs. The Nuggets' head coach [[George Karl]], said Kleiza played fewer minutes because he is not a playmaker.{{cite web |title=Karl enjoying Nuggets' time in sunshine |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2009/05/16/karl-enjoying-nuggets-time-in-sunshine/ |website=The Denver Post |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=May 16, 2009}} ===Olympiacos=== On August 10, 2009, Kleiza agreed to a two-year, $12.2 million ([[Euro|€]]8.6 million euros) [[gross income]] contract with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].{{cite web |last1=King |first1=Jay |title=Linas Kleiza Signs With Greece's Olympiakos |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/233612-linas-kleiza-signs-with-greeces-olympiakos |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090813122044/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/233612-linas-kleiza-signs-with-greeces-olympiakos |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 13, 2009 |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=August 10, 2009}}{{cite web |title=Kleiza signs deal with Olympiakos |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4389053 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=August 10, 2009}} He averaged 17.2 points per game and grabbed 6.4 rebounds per game in the [[EuroLeague]], reaching the [[2010 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague Finals]] with the Reds. Kleiza led the league in scoring, thus winning the [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]], becoming the first Lithuanian to do so. In December 2009, Kleiza was selected the [[Lithuanian Basketball Player of the Year]] (2009) for the first time.{{cite web |title=Geriausi 2009 metų krepšininkai — L.Kleiza ir G.Petronytė |url=https://www.delfi.lt/krepsinis/naujienos/geriausi-2009-metu-krepsininkai-lkleiza-ir-gpetronyte-26860529 |website=[[DELFI]] |access-date=23 January 2026 |language=lt}} ===Toronto Raptors=== On July 7, 2010, Kleiza terminated his contract with Olympiacos. He was signed by the [[Toronto Raptors]] to a four-year, $20 million [[gross income]] offer sheet.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/kleiza_070810.html |title=Raptors Sign Kleiza To Offer Sheet |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 8, 2010 |access-date=July 8, 2010}}{{cite web |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Toronto signs Linas Kleiza to an offer sheet |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2010/07/08/toronto-signs-linas-kleiza-to-an-offer-sheet/ |website=ProBasketballTalk |access-date=March 5, 2020 |date=July 8, 2010}} In December 2010, Kleiza was selected for the second time the Lithuanian Basketball Player of the Year (2010).{{cite web |title=2010 metų geriausi Lietuvos krepšininkai – S. Linkevičienė ir L. Kleiza |url=https://www.tv3.lt/naujiena/sportas/2010-metu-geriausi-lietuvos-krepsininkai-s-linkeviciene-ir-l-kleiza-n517019 |website=TV3.lt |access-date=23 January 2026 |language=lt}} In January 2011, he suffered a serious [[meniscal tear]] in his right knee and was out for the remainder of the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]]. On February 1, 2011, Kleiza underwent [[arthroscopic]] surgery. Kleiza returned to court on January 11, 2012, in a game against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In 14 minutes of game action, he scored 10 points, grabbed 3 rebounds and dished out an assist. On July 16, 2013, the Raptors used the amnesty clause to waive Kleiza.{{cite web |title=Raptors Exercise Amnesty Provision On Kleiza |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-exercise-amnesty-provision-on-kleiza/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130723074539/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-exercise-amnesty-provision-on-kleiza/ |archive-date=July 23, 2013 |date=July 16, 2013}} ===Fenerbahçe Ülker=== On July 26, 2013, Kleiza signed a two-year contract with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. 2016}} ==National team career== [[File:Linas Kleiza against Argentina.jpg|thumb|250px|Linas Kleiza (right) with [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania national team]]]] Kleiza has also played with the senior men's [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuanian national basketball team]]. He played at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] and he won the bronze medal at the [[EuroBasket 2007]] and the silver medal at the [[EuroBasket 2013]]. He also played with Lithuania at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]]. After a poor performance in [[EuroBasket 2009]], Kleiza led his team to a bronze medal in the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], averaging 19.0 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game. He was chosen for the [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. Because of his knee injury, he was not able to help Lithuania at [[EuroBasket 2011]]. ==Executive career== On July 13, 2017, it was announced that Kleiza received part of the [[BC Rytas]] shares from Antanas Guoga.{{cite web|last1=Rimkus|first1=Kęstas|title=Linas Kleiza - apie "Lietuvos ryto" komplektaciją, A.Guogą ir savo, kaip puolėjo, rolę klube|url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/linas-kleiza-apie-lietuvos-ryto-komplektacija-a-guoga-ir-savo-kaip-puolejo-role-klube-875-825756|website=24sek.lt|access-date=July 13, 2017|date=July 13, 2017|language=lt-LT}}{{cite web|title=L.Kleiza tapo "Lietuvos ryto" dalininku ir viceprezidentu|url=http://www.krepsinis.net/naujiena/l-kleiza-tapo-lietuvos-ryto-dalininku-ir-viceprezidentu/275724|website=Krepsinis.net|access-date=July 13, 2017|date=July 13, 2017|language=lt-LT}} He was also named vice president of the club and its sports director.{{cite web|last1=Augustis|first1=Mindaugas|title=Atsakingas pareigas gavęs L.
